analysis:
The only change in this PR for the supplied file is a test comment edit in provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/KVCacheSSD/SSDPrefixCacheTests.swift, at head lines 4361-4363. The comment now says SSDWriteBehind.consume charges the rate-limit bucket per entry in array order only when the whole donation does not fit. The patch changes no executable code.

Units a266c60c7cb77122:5 and :6 are base-side excerpts of the same test file, covering lines 1756-3038. They contain ready-receipt tests, SSDWriteBehind failure barriers, staging reservations and whole-root maintenance tests. These are unchanged context, and none is modified by the patch.

The tests exercise controls described under T-041: ready receipts suppressed on failure, the free-space reserve including pending donation bytes, release of staging reservations, TTL and budget eviction, and kv3 root isolation. The comment edit hints at a production behavior change in SSDWriteBehind.consume, where the donation is admitted whole when it fits and charged per entry only when it does not. That source change is not in this batch, so I cannot assess it.

No security regression is identifiable from the test-only comment change. A reviewer of the production SSDWriteBehind/SSDWriteRateLimiter change, if one exists elsewhere in the PR, should confirm that the all-or-nothing rate-limit admission still keeps ready receipts and durability gated on authenticated rereads, and that the T-041 write-endurance and disk guards remain intact. This is an integration question, not a finding.
